It utilizes a continuously updated cross-scale context that allows for the dynamic representation of urban information, from city planning to individual structures. By initializing from user descriptions, HoloWorld generates urban exteriors and interiors that maintain a strong correspondence, ensuring that the design of indoor spaces reflects the characteristics of their outdoor counterparts. The framework has shown significant improvements in urban generation performance, surpassing state-of-the-art methods while maintaining continuity across different urban blocks.

zh.title: 统一室内外生成的3D城市框架
zh.desc: HoloWorld是一个统一的室内外3D城市生成框架，通过持续更新的跨尺度上下文，确保建筑级别的一致性和跨区块的连续性。该框架从用户描述初始化，逐步表示和更新城市规模到单个建筑的多样化信息，使生成的室内与外部建筑保持明确的对应关系。HoloWorld自回归地生成城市外观，确保跨区块的一致空间组织和视觉特征。实验结果表明，HoloWorld在城市外观生成性能上优于现有技术，显著提高了平均AQS分数，并在统一的3D城市世界中保持强大的建筑级室内外对应关系和跨区块连续性。

papers.title: Knowing What Not to Answer: Selective Non-Compliance in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract KoNA evaluates vision-language models on selective refusal across mixed queries and improves compliance via targeted fine-tuning.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Vision-language models (VLMs) are expected to respond helpfully to appropriate requests while withholding compliance with requests that are incorrect, unsafe, infeasible, or unanswerable. However, existing benchmarks predominantly evaluate non-compliance at the level of the query as a whole, assuming that each request either warrants compliance or requires withholding compliance. In practice, real-world queries can contain a mixture of answerable content and components for which compliance should be withheld. In this paper, we introduce KoNA, a benchmark for evaluating selective non-compliance in VLMs across five categories: False Premise, Visual Inaccessibility, Universal Unknown, Task Feasibility, and Safety. Each task evaluates two capabilities: query-level non-compliance and component-level non-compliance under paired single and compound queries. Our evaluation across diverse VLMs shows that models often fail to refuse, correct, or abstain appropriately, and these failures become more pronounced when queries require selective non-compliance. To address this challenge, we fine-tune VLMs using KoNA examples that require selective non-compliance, together with a fully answerable set that should receive direct answers. Our fine-tuned models achieve substantial improvements in non-compliance accuracy while largely maintaining performance on fully answerable tasks. These results suggest that the fine-tuned models can distinguish between answerable components and those requiring non-compliance and respond in a task-appropriate manner.

ru.title: Избирательный отказ в смешанных запросах: оценка и улучшение VLM
ru.desc: В статье представлен бенчмарк KoNA для оценки способности визуально-языковых моделей к избирательному отказу в выполнении запросов, которые содержат как надлежащий, так и недопустимый контент. Авторы показывают, что существующие модели часто не справляются с задачей различения отдельных компонентов запроса, когда требуется выполнить одни части и отклонить другие. Для решения этой проблемы исследователи применили целевую тонкую настройку VLM на примерах из KoNA, что позволило значительно улучшить точность избирательного отказа. Результаты демонстрируют, что после обучения модели лучше различают компоненты запросов и отвечают надлежащим образом в зависимости от типа задачи.

en.title: Enhancing Selective Non-Compliance in Vision-Language Models with KoNA
en.desc: This paper introduces KoNA, a benchmark designed to evaluate vision-language models (VLMs) on their ability to selectively refuse compliance with certain types of queries. It highlights that existing evaluations often overlook the complexity of real-world queries, which can contain both answerable and non-answerable components. The authors demonstrate that many VLMs struggle with selective non-compliance, particularly when faced with mixed queries. To improve performance, they propose targeted fine-tuning of VLMs using KoNA examples, resulting in significant gains in non-compliance accuracy while preserving the ability to answer fully answerable queries.

zh.title: 提升视觉语言模型的选择性拒绝能力
zh.desc: KoNA是一个用于评估视觉语言模型（VLMs）在选择性拒绝方面的新基准。该基准关注模型在处理混合查询时的表现，特别是如何在可回答和不可回答的请求之间做出区分。研究表明，现有模型在选择性拒绝时常常表现不佳，因此我们通过针对性的微调来提高模型的合规性。最终，微调后的模型在拒绝不当请求的准确性上有显著提升，同时在完全可回答的任务上保持了良好的性能。

papers.title: Refuse without Refusal: A Structural Analysis of Safety-Tuning Responses for Reducing False Refusals in Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract Decomposing safety responses into refusal statements and rationales reveals that training on rationales alone reduces false refusals while preserving safety.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Striking a balance between helpfulness and safety remains a fundamental challenge in aligning large language models. To achieve this balance, models should refuse harmful queries (e.g., "How do I shoot someone?") while remaining responsive to benign inputs, even those superficially resembling harmful queries (e.g., "Where can I shoot a good photo?"). However, models often struggle to distinguish genuinely harmful queries from benign queries that contain superficially risky language, resulting in false refusals. In this paper, we address the issue by decomposing a response in the safety-tuning dataset into two distinct components: (i) a boilerplate refusal statement and (ii) a rationale explaining the refusal. Our experiments and analyses show that refusal statements impede accurate discrimination between harmful and benign queries by inducing reliance on superficial cues. In contrast, training solely on rationales reduces false refusals while maintaining a comparable level of safety performance. Rationale-Only benefits also appear in our ICL configuration and remain compatible with the evaluated inference-time mitigation methods. The results emphasize the necessity of precisely curated, fine-grained safety supervision datasets and outline directions for constructing aligned agents that better reconcile helpfulness with safety.

ru.title: Почему объяснения важнее отказов в безопасности LLM
ru.desc: В этой работе исследователи разделяют ответы моделей при обучении безопасности на два компонента: стандартные отказы и обоснования. Они показывают, что стандартные фразы отказа заставляют модель полагаться на поверхностные признаки языка, что приводит к ложным отказам. Обучение только на обоснованиях (rationale-only подход) снижает количество ложных отказов при сохранении уровня безопасности. Результаты демонстрируют важность точной разметки данных для обучения с подкреплением и помогают создавать более сбалансированные модели, которые одновременно полезны и безопасны.

en.title: Balancing Helpfulness and Safety in Language Models
en.desc: This paper explores how to improve the safety of large language models by separating safety responses into refusal statements and rationales. It finds that training models only on rationales helps reduce false refusals, which occur when a model incorrectly denies a benign query. The authors argue that traditional refusal statements can lead to confusion, causing models to misinterpret harmless questions as harmful. Their findings suggest that better-designed safety datasets are crucial for creating models that can effectively balance helpfulness and safety.

zh.title: 平衡有用性与安全性的关键在于理由训练
zh.desc: 本文探讨了如何在大型语言模型中平衡有用性和安全性。研究表明，将安全响应分解为拒绝声明和理由可以减少错误拒绝，同时保持安全性。通过仅在理由上进行训练，可以提高模型对有害查询和无害查询的区分能力。结果强调了精心策划的安全监督数据集的重要性，以构建更好地协调有用性与安全性的智能体。

papers.title: The 2026 PNPL Competition: Word Classification and Efficient Cross-Subject Generalisation in LibriBrain100
papers.abstract: Abstract The 2026 PNPL competition introduces cross-subject and within-subject word classification tracks using an expanded MEG dataset to advance non-invasive speech-decoding brain-computer interfaces toward clinical feasibility.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small The ambition of the 2025 PNPL competition (Landau et al., 2025) was to launch a multi-year curriculum for non-invasive speech decoding. Designed to progress from foundational tasks toward the linguistic complexity required for a practical brain-computer interface (BCI), it set the stage with speech detection and phoneme classification tasks. Winning submissions reached F1-macro scores of 95.6% and 73.6% on the respective tasks (Elvers et al., 2026), highly significant advances. This success was built on the LibriBrain dataset (Özdogan et al., 2025), the largest within-subject MEG dataset recorded at the time with {sim}50 hours of data for one subject. However, while within-subject scale drives strong decoding performance, a practical BCI must generalise to new users from minutes of data, not hours.   The 2026 PNPL competition responds to this challenge with LibriBrain100 (Mantegna et al., 2026), an extended LibriBrain dataset with 32 additional subjects ({sim}40 minutes each) plus even more within-subject data ({sim}80 hours). Advancing the curriculum of tasks to focus on word classification, two complementary tracks are presented in this competition: the Deep track targets within-subject word classification at scale, aiming at the best possible performance; the Broad track targets cross-subject generalisation, progressively reducing the amount of subject-specific fine-tuning data from {sim}40 to {sim}20 to {sim}10 minutes, a duration that falls within a clinically feasible range and brings us a step closer to a non-invasive BCI capable of restoring communication to people living with profound paralysis.

ru.title: От скальпа к словам: неинвазивное декодирование речи для практических нейроинтерфейсов
ru.desc: Конкурс PNPL 2026 представляет расширенный набор данных MEG для декодирования речи из мозга, включающий две задачи классификации слов: внутри одного субъекта и кросс-субъектную. Работа развивает предыдущие достижения в области распознавания фонем и детектирования речи, применяя deep learning методы к новому датасету LibriBrain100, содержащему данные 32 участников. Основной вызов заключается в переходе от высокопроизводительных моделей, обученных на больших объемах данных одного человека, к практическим BCI-интерфейсам, способным адаптироваться к новым пользователям за клинически приемлемое время (~10-40 минут). Конкурс предлагает две трека: Deep track для максимальной точности классификации слов и Broad track для кросс-субъектной генерализации с минимальным объемом персональных данных.

en.title: Advancing Brain-Computer Interfaces for Effective Communication
en.desc: The 2026 PNPL competition aims to enhance non-invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) by introducing new word classification tasks using an expanded MEG dataset. It builds on previous successes in speech detection and phoneme classification, achieving high F1-macro scores. The competition features two tracks: the Deep track focuses on maximizing performance with within-subject data, while the Broad track emphasizes generalization across subjects with limited data. This approach is crucial for developing BCIs that can effectively assist individuals with severe paralysis by enabling communication.

zh.title: 推动非侵入式脑机接口的语言解码
zh.desc: 2026 PNPL比赛引入了跨学科和同学科的单词分类任务，使用扩展的MEG数据集，旨在推动非侵入式语音解码脑机接口的临床可行性。该比赛的目标是从基础任务逐步发展到实际脑机接口所需的语言复杂性，重点在于单词分类。通过LibriBrain100数据集，比赛提供了更多的受试者数据，增强了模型的泛化能力。最终目标是实现一种能够帮助重建与重度瘫痪患者沟通的非侵入式脑机接口。

papers.title: AdaptVPR: Route-Aware Hard Positive Generation for Robust Visual Place Recognition
papers.abstract: Abstract AdaptVPR improves visual place recognition by generating verified synthetic same-place images with diverse appearance changes to train more robust models.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Visual Place Recognition (VPR) localizes a query image by retrieving database images of the same or nearby place, yet its robustness is often degraded by domain shifts arising from illumination, weather, seasonal changes, and dynamic occlusions. One contributing factor is the limited appearance diversity of the same place in existing training data. To address this issue, we propose AdaptVPR, a route-aware generative augmentation framework that constructs same-place hard positives for robust VPR training. AdaptVPR first uses a vision language model to parse scene attributes and estimate editing feasibility, while a rule-based scheduler determines the generation route according to editability scores and risk constraints. The generation process is decomposed into three complementary routes: the Global Appearance Route introduces global scene changes in weather, illumination, and time of day; the Local Occlusion Route inserts plausible dynamic occluders; and the Dual Route combines both types of perturbations to produce more challenging appearance shifts. Each generated candidate is evaluated using a VPR-oriented verification scheme based on geometric consistency and appearance diversity, reducing the risk of structural drift while ensuring sufficient appearance variation. Global candidates are generated once and rejected if verification fails, while Local Occlusion and Dual candidates use verification feedback for limited prompt refinement and regeneration. Using this framework, we construct AdaptCities, containing 160K verified synthetic same-place hard positives. Experiments across multiple VPR baselines and vision foundation backbones show consistent gains on standard benchmarks and substantial improvements under challenging domain shifts, with R@1 gains of up to 9.2%. The source code and data resources are publicly available at https://github.com/chenshunpeng/AdaptVPR.

ru.title: Синтетическое увеличение данных для устойчивого распознавания мест
ru.desc: AdaptVPR — это новая система для распознавания мест на изображениях, которая использует генеративные модели для создания синтетических данных с разными условиями освещения, погоды и времени суток. Фреймворк применяет видео-языковые модели для анализа сцен и генерирует сложные позитивные примеры через три маршрута: глобальные изменения внешнего вида, локальные окклюзии и комбинированные возмущения. Каждый сгенерированный кандидат проверяется с помощью верификационной схемы на основе геометрической консистентности и разнообразия внешнего вида, чтобы избежать структурных деградаций. Метод показывает устойчивые улучшения на стандартных бенчмарках и достигает прироста метрики R@1 до 9.2% в условиях экстремальных сдвигов в доменах.

en.title: Enhancing Place Recognition with Diverse Synthetic Images
en.desc: AdaptVPR enhances visual place recognition by creating verified synthetic images that show the same location under various conditions. This approach addresses the problem of limited diversity in training data, which can weaken model performance due to changes in lighting, weather, and other factors. The framework uses a vision language model to assess scene attributes and employs a rule-based scheduler to guide the generation of images through different routes, ensuring a wide range of appearance variations. By generating a large dataset of 160K synthetic images, AdaptVPR significantly improves the robustness of VPR models against domain shifts, achieving notable performance gains in standard benchmarks.

zh.title: 通过合成图像提升视觉地点识别的鲁棒性
zh.desc: AdaptVPR通过生成经过验证的合成同地点图像，改善了视觉地点识别的效果。这些合成图像具有多样的外观变化，帮助训练更强大的模型。该方法使用视觉语言模型解析场景属性，并通过规则调度器确定生成路线，以应对不同的编辑需求。最终，AdaptVPR构建了一个包含16万张经过验证的合成同地点图像的数据集，显著提高了在各种挑战性领域转移下的识别性能。

papers.title: Real-World Knowledge-Guided Change Data Synthesis for Remote Sensing
papers.abstract: Abstract KnowChange uses vision-language models to guide flexible, diverse change data synthesis for improving change detection training.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Change data synthesis provides a cost-effective solution for expanding training data and improving the performance of change detection models. However, existing synthesis methods typically rely on handcrafted rules to simulate changes, where limited coverage of class transitions restricts the diversity of synthesized data, while predefined transition designs limit their flexibility in accommodating varied change types. In this work, we introduce KnowChange, a knowledge-guided change data synthesis framework that leverages pretrained vision-language models as knowledge sources to reason about plausible change locations and class transitions from pre-change scenes and desired change types. By integrating knowledge-guided change simulation with generalizable synthesis models, KnowChange enables flexible synthesis of diverse change types within a unified framework. Extensive experiments demonstrate that KnowChange-generated data consistently outperforms existing synthetic datasets in both synthetic-to-real transfer and synthetic data augmentation, despite being generated at a compact scale. Further analyses show that the knowledge-guided change simulation can be seamlessly integrated into existing synthesis pipelines and enhance the downstream utility of synthesized data.

ru.title: Синтез данных об изменениях через знания vision-language моделей
ru.desc: KnowChange — это фреймворк для синтеза данных об изменениях, использующий предобученные vision-language модели как источник знаний для создания реалистичных данных детектирования изменений. Вместо использования жестких правил, метод рассуждает о вероятных местах изменений и переходах классов на основе исходных сцен и желаемых типов изменений. Интеграция знаниевого моделирования изменений с обобщаемыми синтетическими моделями позволяет гибко синтезировать разнообразные типы изменений в единой системе. Экспериментально доказано, что синтетические данные KnowChange превосходят существующие датасеты как при трансфере знаний, так и при аугментации данных для обучения моделей детектирования изменений.

en.title: Empowering Change Detection with Knowledge-Guided Data Synthesis
en.desc: KnowChange is a framework that uses vision-language models to create diverse and flexible synthetic data for change detection training. Traditional methods often rely on fixed rules, which limit the variety of changes that can be simulated. By using knowledge from pretrained models, KnowChange can intelligently generate plausible changes in scenes, improving the diversity of the training data. Experiments show that data generated by KnowChange performs better in real-world applications compared to existing synthetic datasets, making it a valuable tool for enhancing change detection models.

zh.title: 灵活多样的变化数据合成新方法

papers.title: Unfold The World: Factorize 4D Properties in Reinforcing Spatial Reasoning
papers.abstract: Abstract FactoSR improves vision-language model spatial reasoning by decomposing 3D and temporal recovery into factorized geometric sub-objectives optimized via reinforcement learning.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Despite the remarkable prowess of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in general multimodal tasks, they remain fundamentally ``flat'' when reasoning about the physical world. We argue that this spatial bottleneck stems from a profound dimensional mismatch: while VLMs are trained to interpret 2D projections, true spatial reasoning demands the recovery of latent 3D geometry and temporal continuity. To conquer this high-dimensional complexity, we advocate a shift from monolithic learning to a ``divide and conquer'' paradigm. We present FactoSR, a factorized reinforcement learning framework that explicitly interpret the dimensions collapsed by visual projection. At its core, FactoSR decomposes the monolithic problem of world-consistent reasoning into three orthogonal, geometric sub-objectives: planar correspondence (XY), depth consistency (Z), and temporal reversibility (T). By optimizing these verifiable constraints within a unified policy learning mechanism, we effectively transform an ill-posed projection recovery problem into a series of tangible reasoning steps. Extensive evaluations on multi-view and video benchmarks demonstrate that this elegant decomposition yields substantial gains in 3D and 4D reasoning, achieving a 5.9% boost on VSI-Bench and 4.5% on All-Angles-Bench. Our findings suggest that reinforcing explicit, factorized 4D consistency is a critical step toward evolving VLMs into robust, world-aware reasoners.

en.title: Factorized Learning for Enhanced Spatial Reasoning in VLMs
en.desc: FactoSR enhances the spatial reasoning capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) by breaking down complex 3D and temporal tasks into simpler geometric objectives. This approach addresses the limitations of VLMs, which typically operate in 2D, by focusing on recovering latent 3D geometry and maintaining temporal continuity. By employing a reinforcement learning framework, FactoSR optimizes three key aspects: planar correspondence, depth consistency, and temporal reversibility. The results show significant improvements in reasoning accuracy, indicating that a factorized approach is essential for developing more sophisticated and world-aware VLMs.
